sentences.text: Athabascasaurus was a medium-sized ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur that grew to a length of 3.5 meters.
A unique feature of this genus is that each postfrontal bone bears a triangular projection extending over the adjacent postorbital bone.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — had only 42 vertebrae in front of the hips, an unusually low number for ophthalmosaurs, measuring 1.509 meters in length.
The holotype specimen was collected in 2000 from an open-pit mine near Fort McMurray, Alberta.
The genus was first named by Patrick S. Druckenmiller and Erin E. Maxwell in 2010.
Cladistic analyses suggest Athabascasaurus is most closely related to Platypterygius australis and nests within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
Athabascasaurus lived during the earliest Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
The time range for Athabascasaurus is estimated from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
